chunks: Why has there been no habitation that believed and profited by their faith, except the people of Jonah? When they came to believe, We removed from them the affliction of shame in the world, and made them prosperous for a time.
ai.seo_question: What is the exception to the rule that faith brings reward in the Hereafter rather than removing punishment in this world?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often cited as the sole exception to the general principle that faith (Iman) primarily secures reward in the Hereafter, demonstrating that sincere repentance can avert temporal affliction. The phrase 'until a term' (ila hin) indicates a temporary respite rather than permanent salvation, emphasizing that their faith was genuine but their ultimate fate remained subject to divine decree. This narrative underscores the power of collective repentance to alter divine decree in this world, a concept frequently referenced in supplications for relief from hardship.
